es.R: Así que, pastores, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}:

decisions.choice: therefore, shepherds, hear: the call of verse 7 repeated
decisions.reason: After the long oath of verse 8, the call to hear is given again before the sentence of verse 10.

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 7
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 7 at each level, beginning with a small letter at Literal and Balanced because it continues the sentence of verse 8.

source.text: כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְנִ֨י אֶֽל־הָרֹעִ֜ים וְֽדָרַשְׁתִּ֧י אֶת־צֹאנִ֣י מִיָּדָ֗ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּים֙ מֵרְע֣וֹת צֹ֔אן וְלֹא־יִרְע֥וּ ע֛וֹד הָרֹעִ֖ים אוֹתָ֑ם וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י צֹאנִי֙ מִפִּיהֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥יןָ לָהֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] against the shepherds, and I will require my flock from their hand, and I will make them cease from feeding [the] flock, and the shepherds will no longer feed themselves; and I will rescue my flock from their mouth, and they will not be food for them.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against the shepherds, and I will require {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their hand and make them stop feeding the flock, so that the shepherds will no longer feed themselves; and I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their mouths, so that they will no longer be food for them.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against the shepherds, and I will hold them accountable for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. I will remove them from tending the flock, so that the shepherds can no longer feed themselves. I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from their mouths, and the sheep will no longer be food for them.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am against those shepherds. I will hold them responsible for what has happened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. I will not let them take care of the sheep anymore, and they will no longer feed themselves. I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep from them, and they will not eat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep anymore.

fr.L: Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, [je suis] contre les bergers, et je réclamerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau de leur main, et je les ferai cesser de faire paître le troupeau, et les bergers ne se feront plus paître eux-mêmes ; et j’arracherai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau de leur bouche, et elles ne seront plus pour eux une nourriture.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je suis contre les bergers, et je leur demanderai compte de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau. Je leur retirerai la garde du troupeau, et les bergers ne pourront plus se nourrir eux-mêmes. J’arracherai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau de leur bouche, et les brebis ne leur serviront plus de nourriture.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Je suis contre ces bergers. Je les tiendrai pour responsables de ce qui est arrivé à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons. Je ne les laisserai plus s’occuper des moutons, et ils ne se nourriront plus eux-mêmes. Je délivrerai {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons, et ils ne mangeront plus {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons.

es.L: Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo [estoy] contra los pastores, y demandaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rebaño de su mano, y les haré dejar de apacentar el rebaño, y los pastores no se apacentarán más a sí mismos; y libraré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rebaño de su boca, y no les servirá más de comida.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: Yo estoy contra los pastores, y les pediré cuentas por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rebaño. Les quitaré el cuidado del rebaño, y así los pastores ya no podrán alimentarse a sí mismos. Libraré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rebaño de su boca, y las ovejas ya no les servirán de comida.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Estoy en contra de esos pastores. Les pediré cuentas por lo que les ha pasado a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas. No dejaré que sigan cuidando de las ovejas, y ya no se alimentarán a sí mismos. Rescataré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas de ellos, y ya no se comerán a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas.

decisions.choice: I will require my flock from their hand: I will hold them to account for my flock
decisions.reason: To require something from someone's hand is to call them to account for it, as with the watchman (33:6). The shepherds are answerable for every sheep.

decisions.choice: I will rescue my flock from their mouth: the shepherds have become like the wild animals
decisions.reason: The shepherds who should have protected the sheep from wild animals have been devouring them themselves. The LORD will rescue his flock from them.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. "Look, I am against" is Ezekiel's phrase for the LORD turning against someone in judgment (5:8; 13:8).

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le Seigneur DIEU :" (L); "Le Seigneur DIEU dit ceci :" (B); "Voici ce que dit le Seigneur DIEU :" (R), with only DIEU under the divine_name setting
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Ezekiel and published Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "Así dice el Señor DIOS:" (L); "El Señor DIOS dice esto:" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el Señor DIOS:" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as the terms note sets it; the oracle that follows takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "demandaré mi rebaño de su mano" (L); "les pediré cuentas por" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The idiom of requiring something from someone's hand is kept word for word at L and stated as accountability at B and R.

source.text: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִי־אָ֕נִי וְדָרַשְׁתִּ֥י אֶת־צֹאנִ֖י וּבִקַּרְתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I, I myself, will search for my flock and seek them out.

en.L: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and look after them.
en.B: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and look after them.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will search for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep and look after them.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, moi, {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je rechercherai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau et je veillerai sur lui.
fr.B: Car le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je rechercherai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau et je veillerai sur lui.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Je chercherai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons et je veillerai sur eux.

es.L: Porque así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo, yo mismo, buscaré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas y cuidaré de ellas.
es.B: Porque el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: Yo mismo buscaré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas y cuidaré de ellas.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Yo mismo buscaré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas y cuidaré de ellas.

decisions.choice: I myself will search for my flock: the LORD will be his people's shepherd
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses the "I": in place of the shepherds who failed, the LORD himself will do their work. The LORD is the shepherd of his people in Psalm 23 and 80:2 and Isaiah 40:11. Jesus takes up this picture when he calls himself the good shepherd who knows his sheep and lays down his life for them (John 10:11-16), and in the parable of the lost sheep (Luke 15:4-7).

decisions.choice: seek them out: look after them, take care of them
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or to examine, and here it is a shepherd's inspection of his flock to see that every sheep is well (compare Leviticus 27:33).

decisions.choice: I, I myself (L); I myself (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the "I". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say "I myself". The formula is as set at 2:4.

decisions.choice: "moi, moi-même" (L); "moi-même" after the verb (B, R)
decisions.reason: French doubles the pronoun with "moi-même"; the plain "moi" before it is not God's possessive and takes no span, as "je" never does.

decisions.choice: "yo, yo mismo" (L); "Yo mismo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The doubled pronoun is Spanish "yo mismo"; "mismo" is not a free pronoun, so it takes no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: כְּבַקָּרַת֩ רֹעֶ֨ה עֶדְר֜וֹ בְּיוֹם־הֱיוֹת֤וֹ בְתוֹךְ־צֹאנוֹ֙ נִפְרָשׁ֔וֹת כֵּ֖ן אֲבַקֵּ֣ר אֶת־צֹאנִ֑י וְהִצַּלְתִּ֣י אֶתְהֶ֗ם מִכָּל־הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָפֹ֣צוּ שָׁ֔ם בְּי֥וֹם עָנָ֖ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: As a shepherd seeks out his flock on the day he is among his flock [that are] scattered, so I will seek out my flock, and I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered there on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

en.L: As a shepherd looks after his flock on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock; and I will rescue them from all the places where they have been scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.
en.B: As a shepherd looks after his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.
en.R: A shepherd goes looking for his sheep when they have been scattered. In the same way, I will look for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on that dark and gloomy day.

fr.L: Comme un berger veille sur son troupeau au jour où il est au milieu de ses brebis dispersées, ainsi je veillerai sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau ; et je les délivrerai de tous les lieux où elles ont été dispersées en un jour de nuée et d’obscurité épaisse.
fr.B: Comme un berger veille sur son troupeau quand il se trouve au milieu de ses brebis dispersées, ainsi je veillerai sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau. Je les délivrerai de tous les lieux où elles ont été dispersées en un jour de nuées et de sombres ténèbres.
fr.R: Un berger part à la recherche de ses moutons quand ils ont été dispersés. De la même façon, je chercherai {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons. Je les délivrerai de tous les endroits où ils ont été dispersés, en ce jour sombre et triste.

es.L: Como el pastor cuida de su rebaño el día en que está en medio de sus ovejas dispersas, así cuidaré yo de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas; y las libraré de todos los lugares adonde fueron dispersadas en el día de nube y de densa oscuridad.
es.B: Como un pastor cuida de su rebaño cuando está en medio de sus ovejas dispersas, así cuidaré yo de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas. Las libraré de todos los lugares por donde fueron dispersadas en un día de nubes y densa oscuridad.
es.R: Un pastor va a buscar sus ovejas cuando se le han dispersado. De la misma manera, yo buscaré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas. Las rescataré de todos los lugares por donde se dispersaron en aquel día oscuro y sombrío.

decisions.choice: a day of cloud and thick darkness: the day of the LORD's judgment
decisions.reason: The words describe the day of the LORD in Joel 2:2 and Zephaniah 1:15. Here they mean the day of judgment that has already come, when Jerusalem fell and the people were scattered.

decisions.choice: when he is among his scattered flock
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "on the day he is in the midst of his flock, scattered". It pictures a shepherd going among his sheep after they have been scattered, gathering them again.

decisions.choice: that dark and gloomy day (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the picture in plain words, and makes the comparison two sentences.

source.text: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֣ים מִן־הָעַמִּ֗ים וְקִבַּצְתִּים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת וַהֲבִיאֹתִ֖ים אֶל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וּרְעִיתִים֙ אֶל־הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאֲפִיקִ֕ים וּבְכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their land; and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the inhabited places of the land.

en.L: And I will lead them out from among the peoples and gather them from the lands and bring them to their own soil; and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
en.B: I will lead them out from among the peoples, gather them from the lands and bring them home to their own soil. On the mountains of Israel I will feed them, in the ravines and in every settled place in the land.
en.R: I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from other countries. I will bring them back to their own land. I will take care of them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys and in all the places where people live.

fr.L: Et je les ferai sortir d’entre les peuples, et je les rassemblerai des pays, et je les ferai venir sur leur propre sol ; et je les ferai paître sur les montagnes d’Israël, près des ruisseaux, et dans tous les lieux habités du pays.
fr.B: Je les ferai sortir du milieu des peuples, je les rassemblerai des pays et je les ramènerai sur leur propre sol. Je les ferai paître sur les montagnes d’Israël, dans les ravins et dans tous les lieux habités du pays.
fr.R: Je les ferai sortir du milieu des nations et je les rassemblerai des autres pays. Je les ramènerai dans leur propre pays. Je m’occuperai d’eux sur les montagnes d’Israël, dans les vallées et dans tous les endroits où les gens habitent.

es.L: Y las sacaré de entre los pueblos, y las reuniré de las tierras, y las traeré a su propio suelo; y las apacentaré en los montes de Israel, junto a los arroyos y en todos los lugares habitados del país.
es.B: Las sacaré de entre los pueblos, las reuniré de los países y las traeré de vuelta a su propio suelo. Las apacentaré en los montes de Israel, en los barrancos y en todos los lugares poblados del país.
es.R: Las sacaré de entre las naciones y las reuniré de otros países. Las traeré de vuelta a su propia tierra. Cuidaré de ellas en los montes de Israel, en los valles y en todos los lugares donde vive la gente.

decisions.choice: I will bring them out and gather them and bring them to their land: the return from exile
decisions.reason: The picture of the flock now gives way to plain words: the LORD will bring his people back from the nations to their own land (11:17; 20:34, 41; 36:24).

decisions.choice: ravines: stream valleys
decisions.reason: The word means a valley with a stream that may run dry in summer, the kind of place where a flock finds water and grass.

decisions.choice: by the streams (L)
decisions.reason: Literal says "by the streams", the water of the stream valleys (m2); Balanced keeps "ravines", the word used for the same Hebrew in 6:3; Readable says "valleys".

source.text: בְּמִרְעֶה־טּוֹב֙ אֶרְעֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם וּבְהָרֵ֥י מְרֽוֹם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֣ה נְוֵהֶ֑ם שָׁ֤ם תִּרְבַּ֨צְנָה֙ בְּנָ֣וֶה טּ֔וֹב וּמִרְעֶ֥ה שָׁמֵ֛ן תִּרְעֶ֖ינָה אֶל־הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: In good pasture I will feed them, and on [the] mountains of [the] height of Israel will be their grazing place; there they will lie down in a good grazing place, and on rich pasture they will feed on [the] mountains of Israel.

en.L: In good pasture I will feed them, and on the mountains of Israel's height their grazing land will be; there they will lie down in good grazing land, and on rich pasture they will feed on the mountains of Israel.
en.B: I will feed them in good pasture, and their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in good grazing land and feed on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
en.R: I will let them eat in good pastures. Their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. They will lie down there in good pastures and eat the rich grass on the mountains of Israel.

fr.L: Dans un bon pâturage je les ferai paître, et sur les montagnes de la hauteur d’Israël sera leur lieu de pâture ; là elles se coucheront dans un bon lieu de pâture, et dans un pâturage gras elles paîtront sur les montagnes d’Israël.
fr.B: Je les ferai paître dans un bon pâturage, et leur lieu de pâture sera sur les hautes montagnes d’Israël. Là, elles se coucheront dans un bon lieu de pâture et brouteront un pâturage gras sur les montagnes d’Israël.
fr.R: Je les laisserai manger dans de bons pâturages. Leurs pâturages seront sur les hautes montagnes d’Israël. Ils s’y coucheront dans de bons pâturages et ils mangeront l’herbe riche des montagnes d’Israël.

es.L: En buenos pastos las apacentaré, y en los montes altos de Israel estará su majada; allí se recostarán en buena majada, y en pastos abundantes pacerán sobre los montes de Israel.
es.B: Las apacentaré en buenos pastos, y su lugar de pastoreo estará en los montes altos de Israel. Allí se recostarán en buenos pastizales y pacerán en pastos abundantes sobre los montes de Israel.
es.R: Las dejaré comer en buenos pastos. Tendrán sus pastizales en los montes altos de Israel. Allí se echarán a descansar en buenos pastos y comerán la hierba abundante de los montes de Israel.

decisions.choice: they will lie down in good grazing land: Psalm 23:2
decisions.reason: The picture recalls Psalm 23:2, "He makes me lie down in green pastures". The LORD gives his flock rest and plenty.

decisions.choice: the mountains of the height of Israel: the high mountains of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 17:23 and 20:40 for Zion, the mountain where the LORD is worshiped. Here it seems to mean the high country of the land in general, since verse 13 names all its mountains.

decisions.choice: "majada" (L); "lugar de pastoreo", "pastizales" (B); "pastizales" (R)
decisions.reason: Naweh is the grazing place where the flock rests; "majada" is the shepherd's word at L, plainer words at B and R.

source.text: אֲנִ֨י אֶרְעֶ֤ה צֹאנִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַרְבִּיצֵ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I myself will feed my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will feed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will make them lie down, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and let them lie down in rest, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep and give them a place to rest, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Moi-même, je ferai paître {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, et {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je le ferai reposer, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je m’occuperai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau et je le ferai reposer, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je m’occuperai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons et je leur donnerai un endroit où se reposer, dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Yo mismo apacentaré {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas, y yo mismo las haré recostar, declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Yo mismo cuidaré de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas y las haré descansar, afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Yo mismo cuidaré de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas y les daré un lugar donde descansar, dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: I myself: the LORD in person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew again stresses "I" (as in verse 11). The LORD does not hand his flock to another; he tends it himself.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH*. Balanced and Readable say "in rest" or "a place to rest" for "make them lie down".

source.text: אֶת־הָאֹבֶ֤דֶת אֲבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְאֶת־הַנִּדַּ֣חַת אָשִׁ֔יב וְלַנִּשְׁבֶּ֣רֶת אֶחֱבֹ֔שׁ וְאֶת־הַחוֹלָ֖ה אֲחַזֵּ֑ק וְאֶת־הַשְּׁמֵנָ֧ה וְאֶת־הַחֲזָקָ֛ה אַשְׁמִ֖יד אֶרְעֶ֥נָּה בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: The lost I will seek, and the strayed I will bring back, and the injured I will bind up, and the sick I will strengthen; but the fat and the strong I will destroy; I will feed it with justice.

en.L: The lost I will seek, the strayed I will bring back, the injured I will bandage, and the sick I will strengthen; and the fat and the strong I will destroy; I will feed it in justice.
en.B: I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but the fat and strong ones I will destroy. I will tend the flock with justice.
en.R: I will look for the lost sheep and bring back the ones that wandered off. I will bandage the ones that are hurt and make the weak ones strong. But I will destroy the fat and strong sheep. I will take care of the flock fairly.

fr.L: La perdue, je la chercherai, l’égarée, je la ramènerai, la blessée, je la panserai, et la malade, je la fortifierai ; mais la grasse et la forte, je les détruirai ; je le ferai paître avec justice.
fr.B: Je chercherai la brebis perdue et je ramènerai celle qui s’était égarée. Je panserai celle qui est blessée et je fortifierai celle qui est malade, mais je détruirai les brebis grasses et vigoureuses. Je conduirai le troupeau avec justice.
fr.R: Je chercherai les moutons perdus et je ramènerai ceux qui se sont éloignés. Je ferai un pansement à ceux qui sont blessés et je rendrai forts ceux qui sont faibles. Mais je détruirai les moutons gras et forts. Je m’occuperai du troupeau avec justice.

es.L: A la perdida buscaré, y a la descarriada haré volver, a la herida vendaré, y a la enferma fortaleceré; pero a la engordada y a la fuerte destruiré; las apacentaré con justicia.
es.B: Buscaré a las perdidas y haré volver a las descarriadas. Vendaré a las heridas y fortaleceré a las enfermas, pero destruiré a las gordas y fuertes. Pastorearé el rebaño con justicia.
es.R: Buscaré a las ovejas perdidas y traeré de vuelta a las que se apartaron. Vendaré a las que están heridas y daré fuerzas a las débiles. Pero destruiré a las ovejas gordas y fuertes. Cuidaré del rebaño con justicia.

decisions.choice: the lost, the strayed, the injured, the sick: the reverse of verse 4
decisions.reason: The LORD does each thing the shepherds failed to do (verse 4). Jesus says that he came to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:10).

decisions.choice: the fat and the strong I will destroy: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate read "I will watch over" (the fat and the strong), a word that differs by one letter in Hebrew. The standard Hebrew text, "I will destroy", is kept: it prepares for verses 17-22, where the fat sheep that push the weak aside are judged.

decisions.choice: with justice: as a just shepherd who judges between the sheep
decisions.reason: The word *mishpat* means justice and judgment. The LORD's care includes judging between strong and weak in the flock (verses 17-22).

decisions.choice: tend the flock (B); take care of the flock (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "feed it"; Balanced and Readable say what "it" is.

decisions.choice: "avec justice" (R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the word "justice" the meaning decision names, for the shepherd who judges between the sheep (verses 17-22); it is plain enough for Readable.

decisions.choice: "las apacentaré" (L); "Pastorearé el rebaño" (B); "Cuidaré del rebaño" (R); "con justicia" at every level
decisions.reason: Mishpat here is the just shepherd who judges between his sheep (verse 17), so "justicia" rather than "derecho".

source.text: וְאַתֵּ֣נָה צֹאנִ֔י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י שֹׁפֵט֙ בֵּֽין־שֶׂ֣ה לָשֶׂ֔ה לָאֵילִ֖ים וְלָעַתּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, my flock, thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] judging between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.

en.L: And as for you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] judging between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.
en.B: As for you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.
en.R: And now I speak to you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock. This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to judge between one sheep and another, and between rams and male goats.

fr.L: Et vous, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, [je] juge entre brebis et brebis, entre béliers et boucs.
fr.B: Quant à vous, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je vais juger entre une brebis et une autre, entre les béliers et les boucs.
fr.R: Et maintenant, je m’adresse à vous, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau. Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Je vais juger entre un mouton et un autre, entre les béliers et les boucs.

es.L: Y en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, rebaño {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo juzgo entre oveja y oveja, entre carneros y machos cabríos.
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, rebaño {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: Yo voy a juzgar entre unas ovejas y otras, entre los carneros y los machos cabríos.
es.R: Y ahora {{plural_you:les hablo a ustedes|os hablo a vosotras}}, rebaño {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Voy a juzgar entre unas ovejas y otras, y entre los carneros y los machos cabríos.

decisions.choice: I will judge between sheep and sheep: judgment within the flock
decisions.reason: The LORD turns from the shepherds to the flock itself. Not all the people are victims; some, the strong, have abused the weak (verses 18-21). Jesus uses a similar picture of the judgment, when the Son of Man separates the sheep from the goats (Matthew 25:31-33).

decisions.choice: rams and male goats: the strong leaders of the flock
decisions.reason: Rams and male goats lead the flock and can push the others aside. They stand for the powerful among the people.

decisions.choice: the formula inside the address (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4, here after "As for you, my flock", with a small letter at Literal and Balanced. Readable makes the address a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, rebaño mío", with plural "you" to the flock through verse 22
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses the flock with a feminine plural; Spanish follows the ovejas with feminine "vosotras" in the alternative.

source.text: הַמְעַ֣ט מִכֶּ֗ם הַמִּרְעֶ֤ה הַטּוֹב֙ תִּרְע֔וּ וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ מִרְעֵיכֶ֔ם תִּרְמְס֖וּ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֑ם וּמִשְׁקַע־מַ֣יִם תִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וְאֵת֙ הַנּ֣וֹתָרִ֔ים בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְפֹּשֽׂוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: Is it too little for you that the good pasture you graze, but the rest of your pasture you trample with your feet, and clear water you drink, but the rest you foul with your feet?

en.L: Is it too little for you that you graze on the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet; and that you drink the clear water, that you must muddy the rest with your feet?
en.B: Is it not enough for you to graze on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture underfoot? Is it not enough that you drink clear water? Must you also stir up the rest with your feet and make it muddy?
en.R: You eat the best grass. Is that not enough for you? Why do you also trample the rest of the grass with your feet? You drink the clear water. Is that not enough? Why do you also make the rest of it muddy with your feet?

fr.L: Est-ce trop peu pour vous de paître le bon pâturage, qu’il vous faille fouler de vos pieds le reste de votre pâturage ; et de boire l’eau limpide, qu’il vous faille troubler le reste avec vos pieds ?
fr.B: Ne vous suffit-il pas de paître le bon pâturage ? Faut-il encore que vous piétiniez le reste de votre pâturage ? Ne vous suffit-il pas de boire l’eau limpide ? Faut-il encore que vous remuiez le reste avec vos pieds pour la rendre boueuse ?
fr.R: Vous mangez la meilleure herbe. Cela ne vous suffit pas ? Pourquoi piétinez-vous aussi le reste de l’herbe ? Vous buvez l’eau claire. Cela ne vous suffit pas ? Pourquoi rendez-vous aussi le reste de l’eau boueuse avec vos pieds ?

es.L: ¿Es poco para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} que {{plural_you:pazcan|paciáis}} en el buen pasto, para que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} que pisotear con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies el resto de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pastos; y que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}} el agua clara, para que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} que enturbiar el resto con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies?
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:les basta|os basta}} con pacer en el buen pasto? ¿{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} también que pisotear el resto de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pastos? ¿No {{plural_you:les basta|os basta}} con beber agua clara? ¿{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} también que revolver el resto con {{plural_you:sus pies|vuestros pies}} y enturbiarla?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes se comen|Vosotras os coméis}} la mejor hierba. ¿No {{plural_you:les basta|os basta}} con eso? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:pisotean|pisoteáis}} también con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} patas el resto de la hierba? {{plural_you:Beben|Bebéis}} el agua clara. ¿No {{plural_you:les basta|os basta}}? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:enturbian|enturbiáis}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} patas el resto del agua?

decisions.choice: you trample the rest: the strong spoil what the weak need
decisions.reason: The strong sheep take the best for themselves and then ruin what is left. The picture is of the powerful among the people who exploit the poor (22:29).

decisions.choice: is it too little for you: is it not enough
decisions.reason: The question means that taking the best was already too much; spoiling the rest is worse still (compare 16:20, 47).

decisions.choice: two questions made four (B); short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question into four short ones; Readable makes the statements first and then asks.

decisions.choice: four questions (B); short statements and questions (R)
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew questions are split as the English B and R split them.

source.text: וְצֹאנִ֑י מִרְמַ֤ס רַגְלֵיכֶם֙ תִּרְעֶ֔ינָה וּמִרְפַּ֥שׂ רַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשְׁתֶּֽינָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And my flock, what is trampled by your feet they must eat, and what is fouled by your feet they must drink.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, what your feet have trampled they must eat, and what your feet have fouled they must drink.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock must eat what you have trampled with your feet and drink what you have muddied with your feet.
en.R: My other sheep have to eat the grass you have trampled and drink the water you have made muddy.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} brebis, ce que vos pieds ont foulé, elles doivent le manger, et ce que vos pieds ont troublé, elles doivent le boire.
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} brebis doivent manger ce que vous avez foulé de vos pieds et boire ce que vous avez troublé de vos pieds.
fr.R: Mes autres moutons doivent manger l’herbe que vous avez piétinée et boire l’eau que vous avez rendue boueuse.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas tienen que comer lo que {{plural_you:sus pies|vuestros pies}} han pisoteado, y beber lo que {{plural_you:sus pies|vuestros pies}} han enturbiado.
es.B: Y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas tienen que comer lo que {{plural_you:ustedes han pisoteado|vosotras habéis pisoteado}} y beber lo que {{plural_you:ustedes han enturbiado|vosotras habéis enturbiado}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies.
es.R: Y el resto de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas tiene que comer la hierba que {{plural_you:ustedes han pisoteado|vosotras habéis pisoteado}} y beber el agua que {{plural_you:ustedes han enturbiado|vosotras habéis enturbiado}}.

decisions.choice: my flock: the weak are still the LORD's flock
decisions.reason: The weak sheep are "my flock". The LORD takes their side against the strong.

decisions.choice: My other sheep (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "other sheep" to make clear that these are the weak, not those addressed.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הִנְנִי־אָ֕נִי וְשָֽׁפַטְתִּי֙ בֵּֽין־שֶׂ֣ה בִרְיָ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין שֶׂ֖ה רָזָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to them: Here I, I myself, will judge between [the] fat sheep and [the] lean sheep.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to them: Look, I, I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, will judge between fat sheep and lean sheep.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to them: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to them: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi leur parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, moi, {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je jugerai entre la brebis grasse et la brebis maigre.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} leur dit ceci : Je jugerai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} entre les brebis grasses et les brebis maigres.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi voici ce que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} leur dit : Je jugerai {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} entre les moutons gras et les moutons maigres.

es.L: Por tanto, así les dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo, yo mismo, juzgaré entre la oveja gorda y la oveja flaca.
es.B: Por tanto, el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} les dice esto: Yo mismo juzgaré entre las ovejas gordas y las ovejas flacas.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que les dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Yo mismo juzgaré entre las ovejas gordas y las flacas.

decisions.choice: between the fat sheep and the lean: between oppressors and oppressed
decisions.reason: The fat sheep are those who have grown rich at the expense of the poor; the lean are those they have pushed aside.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Literal keeps the doubled "I" as "I, I myself"; Balanced and Readable say "I myself", as in verse 11.

source.text: יַ֗עַן בְּצַ֤ד וּבְכָתֵף֙ תֶּהְדֹּ֔פוּ וּבְקַרְנֵיכֶ֥ם תְּנַגְּח֖וּ כָּל־הַנַּחְל֑וֹת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִיצוֹתֶ֛ם אוֹתָ֖נָה אֶל־הַחֽוּצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Because with side and with shoulder you push, and with your horns you butt all the weak until you have scattered them outside,

en.L: Because you push with side and shoulder, and butt all the weak with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,
en.B: Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak with your horns until you have driven them away,
en.R: You push with your sides and shoulders. You butt all the weak sheep with your horns until you have driven them away.

fr.L: Parce que vous poussez du flanc et de l’épaule, et que vous frappez de vos cornes toutes les faibles jusqu’à ce que vous les ayez dispersées au-dehors,
fr.B: Parce que vous bousculez du flanc et de l’épaule, et que vous frappez de vos cornes toutes les brebis faibles jusqu’à les avoir chassées au loin,
fr.R: Vous poussez avec vos flancs et vos épaules. Vous frappez avec vos cornes tous les moutons faibles jusqu’à ce que vous les ayez chassés au loin.

es.L: Por cuanto {{plural_you:empujan|empujáis}} con el costado y con el hombro, y {{plural_you:acornean|corneáis}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuernos a todas las débiles hasta que las {{plural_you:han echado|habéis echado}} fuera,
es.B: Por cuanto {{plural_you:empujan|empujáis}} con el costado y con el hombro, y {{plural_you:embisten|embestís}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuernos a todas las débiles hasta echarlas lejos,
es.R: {{plural_you:Empujan|Empujáis}} con el costado y con el hombro. {{plural_you:Embisten|Embestís}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuernos a todas las ovejas débiles hasta echarlas lejos.

decisions.choice: you push and butt the weak until you have scattered them
decisions.reason: The strong have done to the weak what the enemy did to the whole people: scattered them. The picture is of the rich and powerful who drove the poor from their land and livelihood.

decisions.choice: Because ... (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 22, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma; Readable makes the charges a sentence of their own.

source.text: וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י לְצֹאנִ֔י וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ינָה ע֖וֹד לָבַ֑ז וְשָׁ֣פַטְתִּ֔י בֵּ֥ין שֶׂ֖ה לָשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: I will save my flock, and they will no longer be prey, and I will judge between sheep and sheep.

en.L: And I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and they will be prey no longer; and I will judge between sheep and sheep.
en.B: I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between one sheep and another.
en.R: So I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sheep. No one will attack them anymore. I will judge between one sheep and another.

fr.L: Et je sauverai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, et elles ne seront plus une proie ; et je jugerai entre brebis et brebis.
fr.B: Je sauverai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, et elles ne seront plus pillées. Je jugerai entre une brebis et une autre.
fr.R: Alors je sauverai {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} moutons. Plus personne ne les attaquera. Je jugerai entre un mouton et un autre.

es.L: yo salvaré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas, y no serán más presa; y juzgaré entre oveja y oveja.
es.B: yo salvaré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas, y ya no serán saqueadas. Juzgaré entre unas ovejas y otras.
es.R: Por eso salvaré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas. Nadie volverá a atacarlas. Juzgaré entre unas ovejas y otras.

decisions.choice: I will save my flock ... I will judge between sheep and sheep
decisions.reason: The LORD's saving and his judging belong together: he saves the weak by judging those who oppress them.

decisions.choice: plundered (B); attack them (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "prey"; Balanced and Readable say what it means for the people.

source.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם רֹעֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וְרָעָ֣ה אֶתְהֶ֔ן אֵ֖ת עַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֑יד ה֚וּא יִרְעֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם וְהֽוּא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ן לְרֹעֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will raise up over them one shepherd, and he will feed them, my servant David; he will feed them, and he will be their shepherd.

en.L: And I will raise up over them one shepherd, and he will feed them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David; he will feed them, and he will become a shepherd for them.
en.B: I will set over them one shepherd, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and he will take care of them. He will tend them and be their shepherd.
en.R: I will give them one shepherd, a king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. He will take care of them and be their shepherd.

fr.L: Et je susciterai sur elles un seul berger, et il les fera paître, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David ; lui les fera paître, et lui sera pour elles un berger.
fr.B: J’établirai sur elles un seul berger, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David, et il s’occupera d’elles. Il les fera paître et il sera leur berger.
fr.R: Je leur donnerai un seul berger, un roi de la famille de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David. Il s’occupera d’eux et il sera leur berger.

es.L: Y levantaré sobre ellas un solo pastor, y él las apacentará: {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David; él las apacentará, y él será su pastor.
es.B: Pondré sobre ellas un solo pastor, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David, y él cuidará de ellas. Las apacentará y será su pastor.
es.R: Les daré un solo pastor, un rey de la familia de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David. Él cuidará de ellas y será su pastor.

decisions.choice: my servant David: a king of David's line
decisions.reason: David had died about four hundred years before. The promise is of a ruler from his family who will be a second David, as in Jeremiah 23:5-6; 30:9 and Hosea 3:5. The New Testament sees the promise fulfilled in Jesus, the son of David (Luke 1:32-33), who calls himself the good shepherd (John 10:11). The text itself names no person but "David".

decisions.choice: one shepherd: one king over a united people
decisions.reason: Ezekiel promises that Israel and Judah will again be one people under one king (37:22, 24). Jesus speaks of "one flock, one shepherd" (John 10:16).

decisions.choice: raise up: appoint, bring to power
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah 23:4-5 and 30:9, the verb is used of God setting up a leader. It does not mean raising from the dead.

decisions.choice: servant (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *'eved* is "servant" at every level for the LORD's servant David, as in the published prophets (Jeremiah 33:21, 26). The servant takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: a king from the family of my servant David (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "David" means here (m1), so the reader does not think of David himself coming back, as Readable does in Jeremiah 30:9 and Hosea 3:5.

decisions.choice: "mi siervo David" at every level; R "un rey de la familia de mi siervo David"
decisions.reason: "Siervo" as the terms note sets it for David; R says, as the English R does, that a king of David's line is meant.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וְעַבְדִּ֥י דָוִ֖ד נָשִׂ֣יא בְתוֹכָ֑ם אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, Yahweh, will be their God, and my servant David [will be] prince among them. I, Yahweh, have spoken.

en.L: And I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will become their God, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David [will be] a prince in their midst. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.B: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will be their God, and among them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be prince. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.R: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will be their God, and the king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their ruler. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have said it.

fr.L: Et moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je serai pour eux Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David [sera] prince au milieu d’eux. Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.B: Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je serai leur Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David sera prince au milieu d’eux. Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.R: Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je serai leur Dieu, et le roi de la famille de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David sera leur chef. C’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui le dis.

es.L: Y yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, seré su Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David [será] príncipe en medio de ellos. Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.B: Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, seré su Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David será príncipe en medio de ellos. Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.R: Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, seré su Dios, y el rey de la familia de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David será su gobernante. Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, lo he dicho.

decisions.choice: prince: *nasi'*, Ezekiel's word for the ruler of Israel
decisions.reason: The word *nasi'* means "one lifted up", a leader or chief. It is used of the leaders of the tribes in the wilderness (Numbers 2:3; 7:2). Ezekiel uses it for Israel's kings (12:10; 19:1; 21:30), and in his picture of the future for the ruler of the restored people (37:25; chapters 44-48). He calls the coming David "king" as well (37:22, 24), so the word does not deny him royal rank. It may stress that the ruler is one of the people, under the LORD who is their God: the LORD is God, and David is prince "among them". This is the main note for the word; later uses refer back to it.

decisions.choice: I will be their God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: Half of the covenant formula, "you will be my people, and I will be your God" (11:20; 36:28; 37:23, 27). The other half comes in verse 30.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *nasi'* in Ezekiel. "Prince" is a leader, not a king's son. Readable says "ruler", and repeats "the king from the family of" as in verse 23.

decisions.choice: "prince" (L, B); "chef" (R) for nasi', for Ezekiel 34-48
decisions.reason: As the term sheet; "roi" would erase Ezekiel's own word for the ruler.

decisions.choice: "Moi, le SEIGNEUR, j'ai parlé" (L, B); "C'est moi, le SEIGNEUR, qui le dis" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as the term sheet words it; the "moi" before the divine name takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "príncipe" (L, B); "gobernante" (R)
decisions.reason: Nasi' as the terms note sets it for Ezekiel 34:24, 37:25 and 44-48.

decisions.choice: "Yo, el SEÑOR, he hablado" (L, B); "Yo, el SEÑOR, lo he dicho" (R)
decisions.reason: The closing formula as the terms note sets it.

source.text: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֥י חַיָּֽה־רָעָ֖ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיָשְׁב֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ לָבֶ֔טַח וְיָשְׁנ֖וּ בַּיְּעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make with them a covenant of peace, and I will remove evil beasts from the land, and they will dwell in the wilderness securely and sleep in the forests.

en.L: And I will make a covenant of peace with them and banish wild beasts from the land, and they will dwell in the wilderness in safety and sleep in the forests.
en.B: I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of wild animals, so that they can live safely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.
en.R: I will make a peace agreement with them. I will get rid of the dangerous wild animals in the land. Then my people will be able to live safely even in the desert and sleep in the forests.

fr.L: Et je conclurai avec eux une alliance de paix, et je ferai disparaître du pays les bêtes mauvaises, et ils habiteront dans le désert en sécurité et dormiront dans les forêts.
fr.B: Je conclurai avec eux une alliance de paix et je débarrasserai le pays des bêtes sauvages, si bien qu’ils pourront habiter en sécurité dans le désert et dormir dans les bois.
fr.R: Je ferai avec eux un accord de paix. Je débarrasserai le pays des bêtes sauvages dangereuses. Alors {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple pourra vivre en sécurité, même dans le désert, et dormir dans les forêts.

es.L: Y haré con ellos un pacto de paz, y quitaré de la tierra las fieras dañinas, y habitarán en el desierto con seguridad y dormirán en los bosques.
es.B: Haré con ellos un pacto de paz y libraré la tierra de las fieras, para que puedan vivir seguros en el desierto y dormir en los bosques.
es.R: Haré con ellos un pacto que les dará paz. Quitaré del país los animales salvajes peligrosos. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo podrá vivir seguro aun en el desierto y dormir en los bosques.

decisions.choice: a covenant of peace: a covenant that brings well-being and safety
decisions.reason: The LORD promises a covenant of peace again in 37:26, and so does Isaiah 54:10 (compare Numbers 25:12). *Shalom* is more than the absence of war: it is wholeness and well-being, described in verses 25-29.

decisions.choice: I will remove wild beasts from the land, and they will dwell securely: Leviticus 26:4-6
decisions.reason: Verses 25-30 follow the blessings promised for obedience in Leviticus 26:4-13 closely: rain in its season, trees giving their fruit, safety in the land, wild animals removed, the bars of the yoke broken, and "I will be your God". The curses of Leviticus 26 have fallen; now the blessings are promised.

decisions.choice: a peace agreement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for "covenant" here and adds "my people" for the subject, so that the reader follows the change from the flock to the people. "Covenant" is kept at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "un pacto que les dará paz" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish R keeps the word "pacto" used throughout, and says what the covenant brings.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֥י אוֹתָ֛ם וּסְבִיב֥וֹת גִּבְעָתִ֖י בְּרָכָ֑ה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י הַגֶּ֨שֶׁם֙ בְּעִתּ֔וֹ גִּשְׁמֵ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing; and I will send down the rain in its season; they will be showers of blessing.

en.L: And I will make them, and the surroundings of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hill, a blessing; and I will send down the rain in its season; there will be showers of blessing.
en.B: I will make them a blessing, and the places around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hill as well. I will send down rain when it is due; there will be showers of blessing.
en.R: I will bless them and the places around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy hill, and they will be a blessing to others. I will send rain at the right time. It will be showers of blessing.

fr.L: Et je ferai d’eux, et des alentours de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colline, une bénédiction ; et je ferai descendre la pluie en sa saison ; ce seront des pluies de bénédiction.
fr.B: Je ferai d’eux une bénédiction, eux et les alentours de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colline. Je ferai tomber la pluie en son temps ; ce seront des pluies de bénédiction.
fr.R: Je les bénirai, eux et les environs de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sainte colline, et ils seront une bénédiction pour les autres. J’enverrai la pluie au bon moment. Ce seront des pluies de bénédiction.

es.L: Y haré de ellos y de los alrededores de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} colina una bendición; y haré descender la lluvia a su tiempo; serán lluvias de bendición.
es.B: Haré de ellos una bendición, y también de los lugares alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} colina. Haré caer la lluvia a su tiempo; serán lluvias de bendición.
es.R: Los bendeciré a ellos y a los lugares alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} colina santa, y ellos serán una bendición para otros. Enviaré la lluvia en el momento justo. Serán lluvias de bendición.

decisions.choice: my hill: Zion, the hill of the temple
decisions.reason: The LORD's hill is Zion, where his house stands (20:40; Isaiah 56:7). The blessing spreads out from it to the land around.

decisions.choice: I will make them a blessing: they will be blessed and be a source of blessing
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes the promise to Abraham, "you will be a blessing" (Genesis 12:2; compare Zechariah 8:13). Some scholars think the Hebrew has suffered in copying; the Septuagint reads differently.

decisions.choice: I will bless them ... and they will be a blessing to others (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both sides of "make them a blessing" (m2), and says "holy hill" so that the reader sees which hill is meant.

source.text: וְנָתַן֩ עֵ֨ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה אֶת־פִּרְי֗וֹ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ תִּתֵּ֣ן יְבוּלָ֔הּ וְהָי֥וּ עַל־אַדְמָתָ֖ם לָבֶ֑טַח וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּשִׁבְרִי֙ אֶת־מֹט֣וֹת עֻלָּ֔ם וְהִ֨צַּלְתִּ֔ים מִיַּ֖ד הָעֹבְדִ֥ים בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the tree of the field will give its fruit, and the land will give its produce, and they will be on their land securely; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.

en.L: And the trees of the field will yield their fruit, and the land will yield its produce, and they will be secure on their land; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
en.B: The trees of the field will bear their fruit and the land will give its harvest, and they will live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the power of those who made them slaves.
en.R: The trees will produce fruit, and the land will produce crops. My people will be safe in their own land. They will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when I break the yoke they wear and rescue them from the people who made them slaves.

fr.L: Et l’arbre des champs donnera son fruit, et la terre donnera son produit, et ils seront en sécurité sur leur sol ; et ils sauront que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand je briserai les barres de leur joug et que je les délivrerai de la main de ceux qui les asservissaient.
fr.B: Les arbres des champs porteront leur fruit et la terre donnera sa récolte, et ils vivront en sécurité sur leur propre sol. Alors ils sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand je briserai les barres de leur joug et que je les délivrerai du pouvoir de ceux qui les avaient réduits en esclavage.
fr.R: Les arbres produiront des fruits, et la terre produira des récoltes. Mon peuple sera en sécurité dans son pays. Ils sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} quand je briserai le joug qu’ils portent et que je les délivrerai des gens qui avaient fait d’eux des esclaves.

es.L: Y el árbol del campo dará su fruto, y la tierra dará su producto, y estarán seguros sobre su suelo; y sabrán que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando rompa las barras de su yugo y los libre de la mano de los que los esclavizaron.
es.B: Los árboles del campo darán su fruto y la tierra dará su cosecha, y vivirán seguros en su propio suelo. Entonces sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando rompa las barras de su yugo y los libre del poder de los que los hicieron esclavos.
es.R: Los árboles darán fruto, y la tierra dará cosechas. Estarán seguros en su propia tierra. Sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cuando rompa el yugo que llevan y los rescate de la gente que los hizo esclavos.

decisions.choice: the tree will give its fruit; I break the bars of their yoke: Leviticus 26:4, 13
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:4 promises that the land will give its produce and the trees their fruit, and 26:13 that the LORD "broke the bars of your yoke" when he brought Israel out of Egypt. The return from exile is a new exodus.

decisions.choice: the bars of their yoke: the wooden bars that held a yoke on an animal's neck
decisions.reason: A yoke was a wooden beam laid across the necks of working animals, held in place by bars or pegs. To break it was to set free (Jeremiah 28:10-13).

decisions.choice: those who enslaved them; those who made them slaves
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone work as a slave. Slavery itself is the point here, as in Egypt (Leviticus 26:13), so every level keeps the word "slave" (style guide on *'eved*). The refrain follows the settled wording.

decisions.choice: "et ils sauront que je [suis] le SEIGNEUR" (L); "Alors ils sauront que je suis le SEIGNEUR" (B, R), for Ezekiel 34-40
decisions.reason: The recognition formula as the term sheet words it, with the person and number the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: "y sabrán que yo [soy] el SEÑOR" (L); "Entonces sabrán que yo soy el SEÑOR" (B); "Sabrán que yo soy el SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: The recognition formula as the terms note sets it; "they will know" is plain "sabrán", with no plural_you span.

source.text: וְלֹא־יִהְי֨וּ ע֥וֹד בַּז֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לֹ֣א תֹאכְלֵ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֥וּ לָבֶ֖טַח וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will no longer be plunder for the nations, and the beast of the land will not devour them; and they will dwell securely, and none will make [them] afraid.

en.L: And they will no longer be plunder for the nations, and the beasts of the earth will not devour them; they will dwell securely, and no one will make [them] afraid.
en.B: They will no longer be plundered by the nations, and the wild animals will not devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid.
en.R: Other nations will not rob them anymore, and wild animals will not eat them. They will live in safety, and no one will frighten them.

fr.L: Et ils ne seront plus un butin pour les nations, et la bête de la terre ne les dévorera pas ; et ils habiteront en sécurité, et personne ne [les] effraiera.
fr.B: Ils ne seront plus pillés par les nations, et les bêtes sauvages ne les dévoreront plus. Ils vivront en sécurité, et personne ne les effraiera.
fr.R: Les autres nations ne les pilleront plus, et les bêtes sauvages ne les mangeront plus. Ils vivront en sécurité, et personne ne leur fera peur.

es.L: Y no serán más botín para las naciones, y las fieras de la tierra no los devorarán; habitarán con seguridad, y no habrá quien [los] espante.
es.B: Ya no serán saqueados por las naciones, y las fieras no los devorarán. Vivirán seguros, y nadie los asustará.
es.R: Las otras naciones ya no les robarán, y los animales salvajes no se los comerán. Vivirán seguros, y nadie los asustará.

decisions.choice: they will dwell securely, and none will make them afraid: Leviticus 26:6; Micah 4:4
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:6 promises, "you will lie down, and none will make you afraid". Micah 4:4 and Jeremiah 30:10 use the same words.

decisions.choice: [them] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object that English needs.

source.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י לָהֶ֛ם מַטָּ֖ע לְשֵׁ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יִהְי֨וּ ע֜וֹד אֲסֻפֵ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יִשְׂא֥וּ ע֖וֹד כְּלִמַּ֥ת הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will raise up for them a planting [place] for renown, and they will no longer be swept away by famine in the land, and they will no longer bear the reproach of the nations.

en.L: And I will raise up for them a planting [place] of renown, and they will no longer be taken away by famine in the land, and they will no longer bear the scorn of the nations.
en.B: I will provide for them a land famous for its crops, and they will no longer be wasted by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.
en.R: I will give them land that is famous for its good crops. They will never again die of hunger in their land, and other nations will not insult them anymore.

fr.L: Et je ferai lever pour eux une plantation de renom, et ils ne seront plus emportés par la famine dans le pays, et ils ne porteront plus l’insulte des nations.
fr.B: Je leur donnerai une terre réputée pour ses récoltes, et ils ne seront plus emportés par la famine dans le pays, ni ne porteront plus le mépris des nations.
fr.R: Je leur donnerai une terre connue pour ses bonnes récoltes. Ils ne mourront plus jamais de faim dans leur pays, et les autres nations ne les insulteront plus.

es.L: Y levantaré para ellos un plantío de renombre, y no serán más consumidos por el hambre en la tierra, ni llevarán más la afrenta de las naciones.
es.B: Les daré una tierra famosa por sus cosechas, y ya no los consumirá el hambre en el país, ni tendrán que soportar el desprecio de las naciones.
es.R: Les daré una tierra famosa por sus buenas cosechas. Nunca más morirán de hambre en su país, y las otras naciones ya no los insultarán.

decisions.choice: a planting place of renown: fields and gardens famous for their harvest
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It seems to mean a land so fruitful that it is famous. The Septuagint reads "a plant of peace", which needs a small change in the Hebrew. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: the reproach of the nations: the scorn Israel suffered for its famine and ruin
decisions.reason: The nations mocked Israel for its hunger and defeat (36:15, 30). That shame will be taken away.

decisions.choice: a land famous for its crops (B); land that is famous for its good crops (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the phrase (m1).

source.text: וְיָדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּ֑ם וְהֵ֗מָּה עַמִּי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will know that I, Yahweh their God, [am] with them, and they, the house of Israel, [are] my people, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, [am] with them; they [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the house of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, am present with them, and that the house of Israel is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then they will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, am there with them. They will know that they, the people of Israel, are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Et ils sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, [je suis] avec eux ; et eux, la maison d’Israël, [sont] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors ils sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, je suis avec eux, et que la maison d’Israël est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors ils sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, je suis là avec eux. Ils sauront qu’eux, le peuple d’Israël, sont {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Y sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios, [estoy] con ellos, y que ellos, la casa de Israel, [son] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios, estoy con ellos, y que la casa de Israel es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} su Dios, estoy allí con ellos. Sabrán que ellos, el pueblo de Israel, son {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: I am with them ... they are my people: the covenant formula
decisions.reason: The refrain "they will know that I am the LORD" is expanded into the full covenant promise: the LORD is with them, and they are his people (verse 24; 11:20; 37:27).

decisions.choice: and they will know (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

decisions.choice: "la casa de Israel" (L, B); "el pueblo de Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets it.

source.text: וְאַתֵּ֥ן צֹאנִ֛י צֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתִ֖י אָדָ֣ם אַתֶּ֑ם אֲנִי֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you, my flock, the flock of my pasture, are human; I [am] your God, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the flock of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture; you [are] {{gender:mortals|men}}, [and] I [am] your God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the sheep of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture. You are {{gender:mortals|men}}, and I am your God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock, the sheep I take care of. You are {{gender:human beings|men}}, and I am your God, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Et vous, {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} brebis, les brebis de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pâturage, vous [êtes des] {{gender:êtres humains|hommes}} ; [et] moi, [je suis] votre Dieu, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} brebis, les brebis de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pâturage. Vous êtes des {{gender:mortels|hommes}}, et moi, je suis votre Dieu, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} troupeau, les moutons dont je prends soin. Vous êtes des {{gender:êtres humains|hommes}}, et moi, je suis votre Dieu, dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, ovejas {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}}, ovejas de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} prado, {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}; [y] yo [soy] {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotras sois}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ovejas, las ovejas de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} prado. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} {{gender:mortales|hombres}}, y yo soy {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotras sois}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rebaño, las ovejas que yo cuido. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, y yo soy {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: you are human: the flock is a picture of people
decisions.reason: The word *'adam* means human beings. At the end of the chapter the LORD says plainly that the sheep stand for people, and sets them, mortal as they are, beside himself as their God. Some ancient witnesses, among them the Septuagint, lack the words "you are human".

decisions.choice: the flock of my pasture: Psalm 100:3; Jeremiah 23:1
decisions.reason: The same words are used in Jeremiah 23:1 and in Psalm 100:3 ("we are his people, the sheep of his pasture").

decisions.choice: mortals (L, B); human beings (R), with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The wording settled for *'adam* set against God (Micah 6:8), with "men" as the gender alternative. "Flock of my pasture" follows Jeremiah 23:1 at Literal.

decisions.choice: "êtres humains" (L, R) / "mortels" (B), with "hommes" as the alternative
decisions.reason: French "hommes" is read as men; the inclusive default says "human" plainly, as Ezekiel 1:5 has it.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}" (L, R); "{{gender:mortales|hombres}}" (B)
decisions.reason: Adam here is humankind: the flock is a picture of people. The default says so for women and men; "hombres" is the traditional wording.
